newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION - Tuigamala returns on the wing.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Tuigamala returns on the wing.

text.p: Dublin, Nov 10 - Va'aiga Tuigamala will return to test rugby for Western Samoa on Tuesday night in the position where he made his name with the All Blacks -- the left wing.

The blockbusting 26-year-old, who plays in the centres for Wigan rugby league club and his English rugby club Wasps, has been chosen on the wing for Manu Samoa largely to preserve the tourists' midfield combination.
The test against Ireland will be Tuigamala's 20th international, with the first 19 coming for New Zealand between 1989 and 1993.

Tuigamala showed how much he can offer the tourists when he appeared for the final half hour of their 35-25 win over Munster in Cork yesterday, making several punishing runs and setting up one of Terry Fanolua's two tries.
He is one of four new caps in the Manu Samoa side for their only test of this British Isles tour.
The others are right winger Afato So'oalo, first five-eighth Earl Va'a and No 8 Isaac Feaunati.
Bedford's Junior Paramore, who joined the tour party here today, will start the match on the reserves bench.
Coach Bryan Williams said the side was fairly easy to select, especially since none of the players in test contention were suffering injury.
The only minor setback was the ruling out of reserve hooker Trevor Leota, who is suspended after being sent off for a high tackle against Munster.
"It's pretty close to what we would have chosen at the start of the tour," Williams told NZPA.
"We had a bit of discussion about the midfield situation, but we thought that with Inga's experience at left wing that was the best place for him.
"We also had to consider our midfield combination, that has been going pretty well.
"There was a temptation to split it up, but not much of a temptation."
Tuigamala's selection on the wing leaves Manu Samoa with the established pairing of George Leaupepe at centre, with To'o Vaega inside him.
Tuigamala said he was thrilled about his looming return.
"I'm really looking forward to it," he told NZPA.
"The team spirit with these guys is amazing, it will be great occasion I'm sure."
Va'a's selection at first five-eighth means there will be two players in the Manu Samoa starting lineup with a rugby league career behind them.

Va'a played rugby league in Wellington before switching codes this year, and making an immediate impact. Now, after just one game for Manu Samoa, he is poised to enter test rugby with the vital job of goalkicking.
"Earl has got a maturity about his play that will be a real asset for us," Williams added.
"He takes good options and has a good kicking game -- he has all the right skills for the position. His goalkicking was also very good against Saracens."
Feaunati's selection, which comes as no surprise, completes a rapid rise and caps an excellent season with Wellington.

Williams also predicts big things for blindside flanker Sene Ta'ala, who impressed with his game against Munster. He scored one of the tourists' five tries and was the outstanding forward on the field.

Western Samoa: Veli Patu, Afato So'oalo, George Leaupepe, Va'aiga Tuigamala, To'o Vaega, Earl Va'a, Joe Filemu, Isaac Feaunati, Pat Lam (c), Mark Birtwistle, Potu Leavasa, Sene Ta'ala, Afa Le'uu, Tala Leiasamaivao, Brendan Reidy. Reserves: Mark Fatialofa, Terry Fanolua or Pailate Fili, Va'a Vitale, Junior Paramore, Lama Tone, George Latu/Robbie Ale.
